name: Celsius freeze / 3AC insolvency / stETH depeg — June–July 2022 CeFi credit contagion

window_utc.notes_inline: Acute phase: June 1 (BTC monthly open $31.7k, stETH already at a ~2-4% discount from the May 12 Terra shock) through July 13 (Celsius Chapter 11). Trough June 18 (BTC $17.6k, ETH $880.93). Slow-reveal preamble begins 2022-05-12.

speed: Slow reveal over ~9 weeks (May 12 – July 13), with an acute crash in the middle: BTC -44% June 1->18 (-37% in the final week; -17% in 48h after the Celsius freeze); ETH -55% June 1->18; stETH ground from ~2% to ~7-8% discount over 5 weeks rather than gapping. Institutional failures arrived in weekly installments: freeze June 12, margin calls June 14-15, 3AC default June 27, bankruptcies July 5 and July 13.
summary: Июнь-июль 2022, медленное вскрытие скрытого плеча: заморозка Celsius (12.06), маржин-коллы и дефолт 3AC (~$10B AUM на пике), stETH дисконт до 0.92-0.94 (вытеснение через полупустой Curve-пул), BTC $31.7k→$17.6k (−44%), ETH −55%. Пеги USDC/USDT/DAI ДЕРЖАЛИ; blue-chip DeFi не взял bad debt (Celsius погасил Maker/Aave полностью). Весь урон — кредит, ликвидность и заморозки: каналы, которых модель USDC=1 не видит. Книга SPA на 2026-08: aave_v3 40% / pendle (PT_USDC) 20% / maple 15% / morpho_steakhouse 15% / кэш USDC 10%.

timeline.event: Terra collapse spillover into stETH: 615,980 bETH bridged back from Terra and unwrapped to stETH, sold into Ethereum. Same day 3AC pulls ~$400M of liquidity (127k stETH + 73k ETH) from the Curve stETH/ETH pool in one tx; Celsius pulls ~$380M in three txs. Pool thins, stETH slips to ~0.95-0.96 ETH (Nansen forensics).

Slow reveal, week of June 6-12: Celsius quietly shuffles collateral (large ETH/WBTC withdrawals from Aave into its DeFi wallets), insolvency rumors build; market fears Celsius must dump its ~$450M stETH stake into a pool that cannot absorb it.

stETH trades at 0.9474 ETH on Curve (~5% discount); Curve stETH/ETH pool imbalanced to roughly 75-80% stETH / 20-25% ETH. US CPI print (8.6%) starts a broad risk-off leg; BTC breaks below $29k over the weekend.

Panic day: BTC -12% to ~$22.5-24k, ETH -15-19% to ~$1,200; total crypto market cap closes below $1T for the first time since Jan 2021; stETH prints ~0.93 ETH; largest single-day count of on-chain DeFi liquidation events of the period. Celsius' Maker vault: 278M DAI debt vs 17,919 WBTC collateral, liquidation price $22,584 — dangerously close to spot.

Celsius (night of June 12 ET) pauses ALL withdrawals, swaps and transfers for ~1.7M registered users citing 'extreme market conditions' ($11.8B AUM as of May, ~$8B lent out). CEL token -60% within an hour to ~$0.19.

Celsius defends its Maker vault: adds ~2,000+ WBTC (to 23,962 WBTC), cutting liquidation price to ~$16,582. Meanwhile a 3AC wallet withdraws ~80,000 stETH from Aave and swaps ~38,900 stETH to ETH (~$45M) at a discount to service its ~$264M Aave / ~$35M Compound loans — selling stETH into the thin Curve pool and deepening the depeg.

3AC fails to meet margin calls; BlockFi and Genesis begin liquidating 3AC collateral (~$400M of liquidations reported); Zhu Su tweets 3AC is 'in the process of communicating with relevant parties'. Fed hikes 75bp the same day.

Contagion widens: Babel Finance suspends withdrawals. MakerDAO executes emergency shutoff of the Aave DAI Direct Deposit Module (D3M) — of 200M DAI supplied to Aave v2, ~100M was borrowed by Celsius against stETH collateral. Aave governance moves to freeze the stETH market and pause ETH borrowing (stETH ~6% below ETH).

Curve stETH/ETH pool nearly drained of ETH — the main on-chain exit for stETH is functionally one-sided, so any further forced seller must accept a worse price or OTC discount (3AC ultimately sold stETH at a haircut near the panic peak).

Capitulation trough: BTC prints ~$17,601-17,800 (lowest since Dec 2020; -44% from June 1 open, -37% on the week), ETH prints $880.93; stETH discount peaks ~7-8% (prints in the 0.92-0.94 ETH range across venues).

BlockFi (after ~$80M loss on 3AC) takes a $250M emergency credit facility from FTX. Maple Finance warns its pools may lack cash to meet withdrawals — lenders must queue for borrower repayments; several pools show zero liquid cash; Orthogonal pool has a $10M USDC loan out to frozen Babel Finance.
CoinFLEX pauses all withdrawals (separate $47M counterparty hole, same liquidity spiral).

Voyager Digital issues notice of default to 3AC on a loan of 15,250 BTC + $350M USDC (~$650-675M). Same day a British Virgin Islands court orders 3AC into liquidation (Teneo appointed; reported June 29). 3AC peak AUM ~$10B (March 2022); creditor claims later filed total ~$3.5B, incl. Genesis $2.36B of loans (~$1.2B claim after collateral), Deribit ~$80M.
3AC files Chapter 15 in SDNY; Voyager suspends all trading, deposits and withdrawals.
Voyager Digital files Chapter 11 (SDNY, case 22-10943; >100,000 creditors, $1-10B assets). July 4: Vauld freezes withdrawals.

Celsius finishes unwinding its Maker vault — repays the final $41.2M of the ~$223M+ paid down since July 1 ($183M tranche on July 5), liquidation price drops to $0 and ~21.9k WBTC (~$450M) collateral is reclaimed. Its DeFi debts were defended and repaid in full; DeFi protocols took no Celsius bad debt.

Celsius repays its remaining Aave debt (~$81M incl. final $63.5M USDC), unlocking ~400-416k stETH (~$410-418M) and moving it to a new wallet; by July 13 Forbes tallies >$1B collateral reclaimed from Maker/Aave/Compound against ~$500M+ of debt repaid. Maple's Orthogonal pool later liquidates the defaulted Babel loan: $7.9M realized loss = 3.2% haircut across $244M of pool deposits.

Celsius files Chapter 11 (SDNY): $4.3B assets vs $5.5B liabilities — a $1.19B balance-sheet hole; user deposits $4.72B of the liabilities. Total assets had fallen from $22.1B (Mar 30) to $4.3B. Acute phase ends; Genesis files its $1.2B 3AC claim July 18 (absorbed by parent DCG).

defi_impact.tvl: Global DeFi TVL roughly halved across the May-June contagion: ~$142B (April 2022) to ~$52B by end-June on one common methodology; the steepest leg came May 8-15 (Terra) with a second ~30-35% leg June 8-19. Per-protocol: Aave/Compound/Curve TVL fell both from price decline and from Celsius/3AC withdrawing >$1B of collateral as they unwound; Curve stETH/ETH pool was nearly drained of its ETH side by June 17 (~80/20 imbalance at peak).
defi_impact.bad_debt_usd: DeFi blue-chips took ~zero bad debt from Celsius/3AC: Celsius repaid Maker/Aave/Compound in full (~$500M+ debt, >$1B collateral reclaimed by July 13); 3AC's Aave/Compound positions were unwound/liquidated at market. Realized DeFi credit loss: Maple/Orthogonal pool $7.9M (3.2% haircut on $244M deposits) from Babel's defaulted $10M unsecured loan. The multi-billion bad debt sat in CeFi: Celsius -$1.19B balance-sheet hole, 3AC ~$3.5B claims (Genesis $2.36B lent / $1.2B claim, Voyager ~$675M).
defi_impact.liquidations_usd: On-chain: ~$362M liquidated on Aave v2 across 5,500+ events (32,000+ positions) during the roughly week-long June stress per Aave's own retrospective; June 13, 2022 recorded the largest daily count of DeFi liquidation events in academic samples of the period. Celsius' 278M-DAI Maker vault was defended (never liquidated). CEX futures liquidations ran ~$1B+/24h on the worst days (June 13-14) but granular historical CEX data is paywalled — treat as approximate.
defi_impact.gas: No sustained gas crisis: brief congestion during the June 13 cascade, but overall Ethereum activity contracted and average fees fell to multi-month lows by early July 2022. Contrast with May 2021 or March 2020 — gas was NOT a binding constraint on exits here.
defi_impact.oracles: No oracle failure. Chainlink ETH/USD tracked correctly; stETH markets priced off actual (depressed) market rates, so the depeg transmitted into Aave collateral valuations by design. Key insight: the damage vector was pool microstructure (one-sided Curve liquidity), not oracle manipulation.
defi_impact.withdrawal_freezes: CeFi: Celsius June 12 (19+ months, ~1.7M users, distributions only from early 2024), Babel Finance June 17, Finblox caps June 16, CoinFLEX June 23, Voyager July 1, Vauld July 4, Zipmex July 20. DeFi-adjacent: Maple lenders queued behind borrower repayments June 21+ (several pools at zero liquid cash) — an effective soft freeze without any code-level pause.
defi_impact.protocols_paused_insolvent: MakerDAO emergency-disabled the Aave D3M (June 17); Aave governance froze the stETH market, raised its liquidation threshold and paused ETH borrowing; Lido publicly warned leveraged stakers of liquidation risk. No major DeFi protocol became insolvent; Maple pools impaired (Babel loss realized July).
defi_impact.bridges_chains: No chain halts or bridge failures attributable to this event; Ethereum, and major L2s/L1s remained live throughout (Solana's Solend had a governance scare over a $200M+ whale position June 19-20, same market stress, no loss).

causes.primary: Hidden, rehypothecated CeFi leverage concentrated in illiquid or one-way assets (stETH pre-withdrawals, GBTC, Terra positions) unwinding after Terra's May collapse: Celsius ran demand-deposit liabilities against staked/locked assets (classic maturity/liquidity mismatch), and 3AC was a massively leveraged common counterparty to virtually every major lender (Genesis $2.36B, Voyager ~$675M, BlockFi, BitMEX, FTX, Deribit, Babel).
secondary: stETH's structural one-way liquidity before Ethereum withdrawals: the Curve stETH/ETH pool was the only at-scale exit, so LP pulls (3AC ~$400M and Celsius ~$380M on May 12 alone) plus forced sales mechanically moved the price — a liquidity-microstructure failure, not an oracle failure
Macro tightening bid-removal: 8.6% CPI print June 10 and the Fed's 75bp hike June 15 (first since 1994) accelerated the deleveraging
Opaque CeFi balance sheets — no one could see who was exposed to whom, so every freeze triggered runs on the next lender
Celsius-specific prior losses (Stakehound ~35k ETH, BadgerDAO hack, Anchor/Terra exposure exited near the top) already had it insolvent per later examiner findings
Undercollateralized lending: Genesis' 3AC loans had >80% margin requirements breached; Maple pools lent unsecured to trading firms (Babel via Orthogonal)
causes.mechanism: Terra collapses (May) -> 615,980 bETH unwrapped to stETH and sold + big LPs (3AC, Celsius) pull Curve stETH liquidity -> pool skews to ~80% stETH, stETH slips to 0.94-0.95 -> mark-to-market losses and collateral haircuts on Aave/Maker loans backed by stETH/WBTC -> depositors run on Celsius -> Celsius freezes withdrawals June 12 -> market-wide panic (BTC < $1T cap day, June 13) -> margin calls on 3AC -> 3AC dumps ~39k stETH into the thin pool June 14, deepening the depeg it is being margin-called on -> lenders (BlockFi, Genesis) liquidate 3AC -> 3AC defaults (Voyager June 27) and is court-liquidated -> counterparty freezes cascade (Babel June 17, CoinFLEX June 23, Voyager July 1, Vauld July 4) -> bankruptcies: 3AC June 27/July 1, Voyager July 5, Celsius July 13. Weeks-long slow reveal, not a single-day crash.

contagion: Terra/UST collapse (May 7-13) -> stETH depeg begins (bETH unwind + 3AC/Celsius pull ~$780M Curve liquidity, May 12)
stETH discount -> Celsius (illiquid stETH vs demand deposits) hit by depositor run -> withdrawal freeze June 12
Celsius freeze -> market-wide panic: BTC -12% June 13, market cap < $1T, DeFi liquidation-event record day
Panic prices -> 3AC margin calls June 14-15 -> 3AC dumps stETH into thin Curve pool (reflexive deepening of the depeg)
BlockFi/Genesis liquidate 3AC collateral -> 3AC insolvent -> defaults on Voyager ($675M) June 27 -> BVI liquidation order
3AC default -> Voyager freeze July 1 -> Voyager Chapter 11 July 5; Genesis $1.2B hole absorbed by DCG (resurfaces in Nov 2022 FTX round)
Babel freeze June 17 -> Maple/Orthogonal $10M loan defaults -> first realized DeFi-lender loss ($7.9M, 3.2% pool haircut) + Maple withdrawal queues
Defensive DeFi governance: MakerDAO cuts Aave D3M June 17; Aave freezes stETH market — DeFi protocols de-risk and take no Celsius bad debt (Celsius repays Maker/Aave/Compound in full by July 12-13)
Celsius Chapter 11 July 13 (-$1.19B balance sheet); BlockFi survives on FTX credit line — chain continues into FTX/Genesis collapse Nov 2022

recovery.time_to_recover: stETH: discount ~3% by mid-Aug 2022, re-widened to ~5-7% pre-Merge (Sep 7), effectively closed after the Merge and fully converged after Shapella withdrawals (Apr 2023). BTC/ETH: no V-recovery — ranged $19-25k / $1,000-2,000 through summer; BTC made a LOWER low ~$15.5k in Nov 2022 (FTX), regaining its June 1 2022 level (~$31.7k) only ~June 2023 (≈12 months). ETH's June 18 low of $880.93 held as the cycle low.
recovery.notes: Credit never recovered: Celsius depositors were frozen 19+ months (court distributions began Jan-Feb 2024 at partial recovery); Voyager creditors took years; 3AC claims ~$3.5B in liquidation; Genesis' 3AC hole ($1.2B, papered over by a DCG promissory note) resurfaced and helped fail Genesis in the Nov 2022 FTX round. The June 2022 episode is the middle link of a three-part 2022 chain: Terra (May) -> Celsius/3AC (June-July) -> FTX/Genesis/BlockFi (Nov).

confidence_notes: Directly observed and multi-sourced: freeze/bankruptcy dates (Celsius June 12/July 13; Babel June 17; CoinFLEX June 23; Voyager July 1 & 5; Vauld July 4; 3AC default June 27, BVI order June 27/reported June 29, Ch.15 July 1); Celsius Maker vault mechanics and full DeFi repayment; MakerDAO D3M shutoff; Maple crunch and the $7.9M Babel loss; Genesis $2.36B/3AC and Voyager $350M USDC + 15,250 BTC. Approximate/ranged: BTC trough $17,601-$17,800 (venue differences; StatMuse/CoinMarketCap daily low vs CNBC intraday print) — I use $17,601; BTC June open ~$31,700 is inferred from StatMuse monthly close $19,784.73 at -37.8% (arithmetic implies ~$31.8k open) — drawdown_pct -44.5% carries ~±1pp uncertainty; stETH trough is venue/pool-depth dependent: sourced prints span 0.92 (CoinDesk) to 0.9337-0.94 (Trustnodes and market-data recaps) — I report the range rather than one number; Voyager loan headline varies $650M-$675M purely with BTC marks; 3AC peak AUM ~$10B is Nansen's March 2022 estimate repeated by CNBC (some later reporting suggested up to $18B unverified — not used); global TVL 'April $142B -> June $52B' is one methodology (DeFiLlama recomputations differ; treat magnitudes, ~-60-65%, not exact levels); Aave $362M/32k-positions liquidation figure comes from Aave's own retrospective and the summary may blur May (Terra) vs June windows — medium confidence; CEX liquidation totals (~$1B/24h June 13-14) are news-cycle aggregates, not verified tape. Unsourced -> null: a specific June 2022 USDT low (held near peg; no reliable print found), CEL pre-crash reference price, and any June 13 gas-spike quantification (evidence actually points to falling fees through late June — the gas claim in defi_impact is partly inference). USDC premium during flight-to-quality is inference from its role as settlement asset, not a measured series. The Celsius pre-freeze wallet-shuffling timeline entry (June 7) is from secondary year-in-review reporting — marked observed=false.

spa_relevance.summary: This is the canonical stress for exactly SPA's shape of portfolio: USDC lending against opaque counterparties, receipt tokens with thin one-way exits, and the assumption that 'withdrawable' is a constant. Stablecoin pegs (USDC/USDT/DAI) HELD — every dollar of damage came through credit, liquidity and freeze channels a USDC=1 model does not see.

position_by_position.aave_v3_usdc_supply: Channel: liquidity crunch + APY whipsaw, NOT bad debt. In June 2022 Aave v2 processed $362M of liquidations with no material insolvency, and Celsius/3AC repaid — USDC suppliers lost nothing. But: utilization spiked as stressed borrowers drew stables and suppliers fled; governance froze the stETH market and paused ETH borrowing within days. A replay means: temporarily unable to withdraw full size at will (utilization > liquid reserves), stables supply APY spiking then collapsing as leverage demand evaporates. UNPRICED if the system assumes Aave is always instantly withdrawable at par.
position_by_position.pendle_pt: Channel: receipt-token discount + AMM liquidity evaporation. The stETH 6-8% discount IS the Pendle-PT stress template: a par-convergent claim traded through a single thin pool, where large LPs withdrawing (3AC/Celsius pulled ~$780M from Curve on one day) both removes exit liquidity and moves the price against remaining holders. A PT held to maturity converges, but any forced or rebalancing exit mid-crisis realizes a 5-10% mark-to-market haircut plus slippage.
